acquisitions.reason: Durable execution, persistence and human-in-the-loop remain relevant reference patterns, but the frozen GAP-A10 experiment did not justify a canonical runtime dependency for the current bounded baseline.
acquisitions.next_gate: Do not adopt as production runtime unless a new measured bottleneck and separate governance experiment demonstrate concrete value beyond the framework-independent baseline.

acquisitions.reason: The 2026-07-28 specification provides a stateless core, deterministic/cacheable discovery behavior, explicit extensions and hardened authorization suitable for bounded agent-tool integration.
acquisitions.next_gate: Any MCP server/client added to the project must pass least-privilege, authorization, prompt-injection and write-scope review.

acquisitions.reason: Provides practical patterns for typed/function tools, approvals, guardrails, tracing and an evaluation flywheel that maps directly to RAG and agent regression engineering.
acquisitions.next_gate: Use as a methodology/reference source only; no OpenAI API runtime dependency or paid model call is authorized by this acquisition alone.

acquisitions.reason: Crews, flows, skills and production observability are relevant, but they duplicate orchestration already represented by the SARE specialist registry and would add a second runtime before a measured need exists.
acquisitions.next_gate: Re-evaluate only if collaborative role orchestration becomes a measured bottleneck that the framework-independent GitHub execution model cannot satisfy.

acquisitions.reason: Current framework capabilities include graph workflows, checkpoints, specialized agents, context providers and human-in-the-loop, but they overlap with LangGraph/reference patterns and are not required by the GitHub-only SARE runtime.
acquisitions.next_gate: Re-evaluate if Microsoft/Azure hosting, A2A integration or typed cross-service workflows become explicit project requirements.

acquisitions.reason: Low-code workflow, knowledge and plugin capabilities are useful for application construction, but would create an external orchestration surface inconsistent with current GitHub-only canonical operation.
acquisitions.next_gate: Use only as a non-canonical prototyping surface if later justified by an explicit application-delivery requirement.

acquisitions.reason: RAG is now an implemented SARE capability. Official LlamaIndex Workflows patterns cover RAG plus reranking, citation query engines, corrective RAG, durable workflows, testing and observability, making them directly useful as controlled design and benchmark references without importing the framework.
acquisitions.next_gate: Use the patterns to expand deterministic RAG evaluation and compare retrieval strategies. Any llama-index package dependency requires a separate pinned benchmark, license/security review and measurable improvement over the built-in retriever.

acquisitions.reason: Embedding and reranker models may become relevant for semantic-retrieval experiments, but models and datasets must not be added merely to increase capability count; each candidate needs a predeclared quality gap and reproducible evaluation.
acquisitions.next_gate: Before any model acquisition require model card, exact revision, license, provenance, resource budget, offline reproducibility and measured retrieval gain against the deterministic lexical baseline.

acquisitions.reason: External prompts and chains are untrusted behavior packages until inspected, versioned and regression-tested.
acquisitions.next_gate: Pin exact artifact/version and add agent regression tests before use.

acquisitions.reason: Community collection is useful for discovery but is not an authoritative or vetted supply-chain source.
acquisitions.next_gate: Trace every candidate to its original repository and perform license, maintainer, security and code review.
